title: Geologic Records of High Sea Levels
text: On a tectonically active coast, such as California, changes in sea level are recorded as marine terraces, wave-cut benches that formed in the surf zone during interglacial periods, but are now above sea level due to uplift. Wave-cut benches also form during glacial periods, but these are offshore and underwater during interglacial periods. If uplift is continuous over time, a “stair step” type of landscape develops, as shown here, with each successively higher terrace corresponding to a successively older interglacial period.
